Baidu Baike was created by Baidu founder Robin Li, and was released to the public around 20 April 2006, following the Chinese government's decision to censor Wikipedia in 2005.[11][2][12][3] After 20 days, it had more than 300,000 registered users and more than 100,000 articles, surpassing the number in Chinese Wikipedia.[3]. During the conference WWW2008 of the World Wide Web Consortium, Baidu's William Chang said, "There is, in fact, no reason for China to use Wikipedia ... It's very natural for China to make its own products."[13] When searching with the search engine Baidu, the link to the corresponding entry in Baidu Baike, if it exists, will be put as the first result or one of the first results.[14] The Chinese government has, through the Great Firewall, blocked access to all editions of Wikipedia since 2019.[15][16].
Thought 2: The passage for Baidu Baike mentions that it surpassed Chinese Wikipedia in terms of articles after 20 days of its launch. Action 2: Search[Hudong.com]
Observation 2: Douyin Baike (Chinese: 抖音百科; pinyin: dǒu yīn bǎi kē), formerly known as Hudong Baike (Chinese: 互动百科, also sometimes spelled Hoodong and also known as Baike.com), is a for-profit Chinese-language user-editable online encyclopedia and social network owned by ByteDance. Founded in 2005 in emulation of Wikipedia, it is one of the two largest wikis in China, along with its more prominent rival, Baidu Baike.. Baike.com is a wiki and lets its users edit and contribute material. Frequent users may accumulate credits redeemable for gifts.[1] It has also included features of social networking sites, including chat forums and fan groups.[2][3] Baike.com is a for-profit business partially supported by advertising and paid support services.[2]. Hudong Baike developed its own wiki software platform, called HDWiki, as a rival to MediaWiki.
Thought 3: Hudong.com (now Douyin Baike) is described as "one of the two largest wikis in China, along with its more prominent rival, Baidu Baike." Both Baidu Baike and Hudong.com are "in emulation of Wikipedia". Baidu Baike explicitly states it "surpassing the number in Chinese Wikipedia." Given that Hudong.com is also a major Chinese wiki emulating Wikipedia, and a rival to Baidu Baike, it's highly probable that it also surpassed Wikipedia or at least competed with it. The question asks for the website surpassed by *both*. Wikipedia is the common link. The question then asks "Who runs the website". I need to find who runs Wikipedia.
Action 3: Search[Wikipedia]
Observation 3: Wikipedia[c] is a free online encyclopedia written and maintained by a community of volunteers, known as Wikipedians, through open collaboration and the wiki software MediaWiki. Founded by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger in 2001, Wikipedia has been hosted since 2003 by the Wikimedia Foundation, an American nonprofit organization funded mainly by donations from readers.[1] Wikipedia is the largest and most-read reference work in history.[2][3]. Initially available only in English, Wikipedia exists in over 340 languages and is one of the world's most visited websites. The English Wikipedia, with over 7 million articles, remains the largest of the editions, which together comprise more than 66 million articles and attract more than 1.5 billion unique device visits and 13 million edits per month (about five edits per second on average)  as of April 2024[update].[W 1] As of December 2025[update], over 25% of Wikipedia's traffic comes from the United States, while Japan accounts for nearly 7%, and the United Kingdom, Germany, and Russia each represent around 5%.[4]. Wikipedia has been praised for enabling the democratization of knowledge, its extensive coverage, unique structure, and culture.
Thought 4: Wikipedia is hosted by the Wikimedia Foundation.
Action 4: Finish[Wikimedia Foundation]
Observation 4: Episode finished, reward = 1
